clue.text: Maybe Tripoli wins vote after soldiers charge

indicators.note: the vote piece is placed following the soldiers piece in the answer

parts.note: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, an example of a capital city
to win something is to gain it, so wins gives gains
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper as a vote

explanation.surface: A Libyan capital's election victory follows military action against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts X following TA. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax is a charge levied by the state, here on profits from selling assets.

clue.text: He said "shaken, not stirred" — timeless Bond!

indicators.note: shaken, like a cocktail, signals the letters of these two words are mixed up
stirred, the other way to mix a drink, signals the remaining letters are jumbled
timeless means the word loses its T, the usual abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A quotation of James Bond's famous cocktail order, with his name as the punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges HESAID to ADHESI; 'timeless' takes T from NOT leaving NO, and 'stirred' turns that into ON. The surface is Bond's 'shaken, not stirred' martini order.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a sticking together, and adhesion is the state of things being stuck to one another.

clue.text: Doctor No: "He's cut in half, my dear"

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is read as has, linking the next piece; He gives its own two letters

indicators.note: only the second half of the little word my is kept

explanation.surface: A line of dialogue from the Bond film Dr No, the villain addressing someone fondly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges NOHE to HONE; 'cut in half' keeps the Y of 'my'. Honey Ryder is the heroine of the Bond film Dr No.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate terms of address for a loved one, as in calling someone sweetheart.

clue.text: Crawl into water, good animal

indicators.note: into means the crawling piece is placed inside the water piece

parts.note: water's chemical formula H2O written out as its atoms gives two hydrogens and an oxygen
to edge forward is to move slowly, to crawl

explanation.surface: Advice to creep into water, praising some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; water is taken as its chemical formula H2O written out atom by atom, a liberty some solvers dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedgehog is a small spiny mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Author exhibits Muslim art in a misquote

indicators.note: exhibits means the clue words display the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A writer is shown with a piece of Islamic art and a wrongly remembered quotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibits' shows the run in musliM ART IN A MISquote.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Amis was a British novelist, author of Money and London Fields.

clue.text: Hit maker?

parts.note: a hit maker sounds like a chart-topping producer, but rap means hit, so one who raps is the maker

explanation.definitionFit: A rapper performs rap, and to rap is to strike, so this performer literally makes hits.

clue.text: Artist models clouds

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of the word are reshaped

explanation.surface: A painter makes studies of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' rearranges ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, flat cloud type; this is its Latin plural form.

clue.text: Holiday film?

definitions.meaning: the Fourth of July, the US national holiday celebrating the 1776 declaration
the 1996 alien-invasion blockbuster starring Will Smith

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the American July holiday and a 1996 Hollywood science-fiction movie.

clue.text: Greek maiden with romantic dream about love

parts.note: and means together with, so with gives and

indicators.note: about means the anagrammed piece goes around the love piece
romantic suggests something fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Greek girl has a romantic dream about being in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romantic' rearranges DREAM, and 'about' wraps it round O to make ROMEDA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the princess chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Team building follows when not working

indicators.note: follows means the building piece comes after the rest

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: working suggests the word is worked over, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a villa is a large house, a kind of building

explanation.surface: A team-building exercise happens when people aren't at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' signals the anagram. Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club; 'Team building' reads as one office phrase but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English professional football club based in Birmingham.

clue.text: Titanic problem — Diamonds Are Forever's finale needs £1,000

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
are is a form of the verb to be

indicators.note: finale means the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a grand, a thousand pounds, is abbreviated G

explanation.surface: A Bond-film title, Diamonds Are Forever, with its ending needing a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finale' takes R from Forever. G is a grand, slang for £1,000.
explanation.definitionFit: The liner Titanic sank in 1912 after striking a floating mass of ice.

clue.text: Choose to swallow ace cooked bun

indicators.note: to swallow means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: to take one is to choose it

indicators.note: cooked suggests something tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner opts to gulp down a well-baked bun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals the anagram and 'to swallow' the container; 'Choose' looks like an instruction to the reader but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light, sweet yeast bun with dried fruit, often toasted.

clue.text: See 5
After starting to train women, one church backs reason to doubt

indicators.note: backs means the following pieces stand behind the reason piece

parts.note: to reason is to think something through

indicators.note: starting to means the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: After training begins, a woman and a church give grounds for scepticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'backs' both put the TWICE pieces behind THINK; 'starting to' takes T from train.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate and reconsider before acting is to doubt one's first choice.

clue.text: I wrestle with bear, then sleep

indicators.note: wrestle suggests a tangle, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone tackles a bear and then takes a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestle' rearranges IBEARTHEN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hibernate is to pass the winter in a long deep sleep, as bears do.

clue.text: Shooting weapon at home pierces new bodyguard's heart

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: pierces means the home piece goes inside the following letters
heart means the middle letter of the word is taken

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A weapon shot at a house wounds a new protection officer in the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes G, the middle of the nine-letter bodyguard; 'pierces' puts IN between N and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunning is shooting with guns, as in going out gunning for game.

clue.text: Rushed copper once pursues subtle criminal

indicators.note: pursues means the copper piece comes after the anagram
criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D was the old penny, a copper coin before decimalisation in 1971

explanation.surface: An old-time policeman chases a cunning offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges SUBTLE. 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the coin: D was Britain's pre-decimal penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To bustle is to move busily and hurriedly, so bustled means hurried about.

clue.text: Vegetable oil runs beneath half-broken engine size

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word broken is used

parts.note: engine capacity is measured in cubic centimetres, CC

indicators.note: runs suggests a liquid spreading, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oil leaks from beneath a partly broken engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-' gives BRO from broken; 'runs' rearranges OIL to OLI, and 'beneath' sets it below in this down entry. Cubby Broccoli produced the Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family with tight flower heads.

clue.text: Much laughter over king 10's lover

parts.note: a lot means much
ha is a burst of laughter
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
10 written as letters looks like I and O

explanation.surface: A great deal of mirth over a monarch and his number ten's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is read as the letters IO; 'over' just stacks the pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, after a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Checkpoints? Nice when travelling

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Border controls are encountered when journeying through the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checkpoints' must be split: Check is the definition and 'points' joins Nice as fodder for 'when travelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspection is a careful look over something, a check.

clue.text: Untouchable Spain's No 1, getting measure over Germany

indicators.note: over places the measure above the Germany piece in this down entry
number one means the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an acre is a measure of land area
D is the international vehicle code for Germany, Deutschland

explanation.surface: Spain's top player is untouchable, outscoring Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' takes S from Spain's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred is held holy, so it must not be violated or touched.

clue.text: This hat's 3 pound, yes?

parts.note: tri is the prefix meaning three
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A question about whether a hat costs three pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This hat' refers to the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown, a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Planet loses 10% first of atmosphere and rainforest — wow!

indicators.note: loses means letters are taken out of the planet

parts.note: Saturn is a planet

indicators.note: each of the next two words has ten letters, so a tenth of each is its first letter

explanation.surface: A planet loses a tenth of its atmosphere and forest cover, to astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: '10% first of' gives A and R, a tenth of each ten-letter word; 'loses' takes them from SATURN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to amaze or astonish, much as an exclamation of wonder does.

clue.text: See 10
CD noise spoiled parts of a duet

indicators.note: spoiled suggests damage, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Interference ruins a recording of a duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges CDNOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the secondo is the lower part; this is its Italian plural.

clue.text: 151 + 1000 + 8, say? That's the spirit

parts.note: 151 in Roman numerals is CLI
1000 in Roman numerals is M

indicators.note: say means the word for the number is heard rather than written

parts.note: the number eight

explanation.surface: An odd sum followed by an encouraging exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns EIGHT into ATE by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The climate of the times is its prevailing mood or spirit.

clue.text: Spy a refined male's mature books

parts.note: to age is to mature
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A spy is a gentleman whose library is mature.
explanation.walkthrough: A second charade runs alongside: 'a refined male' is A GENT, joined by 's (is) to this one.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone employed in espionage, a secret operative.

clue.text: Bass's first note sounds like a stringed instrument

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass
A is a top grade, first class
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: sounds means the words are pronounced as heard

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like LAIKA

explanation.surface: A double bass's opening note resembles some other stringed thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' makes 'like a' come out LAIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a Russian folk instrument with a triangular body and three strings.
